discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac showed theoretically (Jaksch et al., 1998, and later work) that cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, and proposed that controllable atomic systems could serve as quantum simulators of problems that classical computers cannot solve. Bloch and co-workers realised this in 2002 by observing the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator. Their subsequent work introduced single-site imaging, artificial gauge fields, many-body localization and Fermi-Hubbard antiferromagnetism. Together these results turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into a laboratory method. They link quantum optics, condensed-matter physics and quantum information, give a common language to several communities and now underpin analog and digital quantum simulators worldwide. This is a clear example of theory and experiment advancing together to open a new field.
